A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FiMO attribution study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures and appendices are readable and matchable despite reformatting, relocation and added material.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original experiments comparing gradient-based attribution with further training across four tabular datasets, CIFAR-10 and SST-2.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds Spearman-correlation results, comparisons with retraining, mislabeled-example detection and qualitative attribution examples.

M1.justification: The further-training objective, adjustment and averaging procedures, and gradient-based approximations remain unchanged. FiMODA names the existing sensitivity-based formulation. Damping settings and the leave-one-out loss implementation highlighted in v2 were already documented in v1's Appendix D.

E1.justification: All six original datasets and modalities remain. Appendix E.2.1 adds a bounded downstream task: detecting deliberately flipped training labels in FICO, Folktables and SST-2. This introduces corrupted-label scenarios within existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The original eight gradient-based methods and their dataset-specific omissions are retained. Figure 11 adds LOO retraining from scratch as an empirical comparison reference on Concrete Strength and Energy Efficiency; no new gradient-based comparator is introduced.

E3.justification: Existing splits, architectures, optimizers and training settings remain. Added evaluation protocols include Spearman correlation across the six datasets, comparison against LOO retraining, and a detection experiment that flips 20% of the selected training labels and evaluates ROC AUC after one further-training epoch. These substantially broaden how attribution quality is evaluated.

E4.justification: v2 adds checks of metric dependence through Spearman correlation, contrasts approximation of further training with retraining from scratch, tests alignment with mislabeled-example detection, and examines influential Folktables and SST-2 examples. These extend the original optimizer, adjustment, averaging and attribution-shape analyses.

E5.justification: The main experiments retain 100-seed averaging and standard-error reporting. Appendix D.3 newly specifies seeds 0–99, while Appendix E.2.1 documents 40 trials with mean and standard error for the new detection experiment. This does not establish an increase in runs for existing experiments.

E6.justification: Original result plots are retained, including relocated figures. New results include Spearman curves, near-zero cosine similarity to retraining on the two regression datasets, and qualitative examples. Detection AUCs are newly reported as 0.758 ± 0.008 for FICO, 0.627 ± 0.012 for Folktables and 0.995 ± 0.003 for SST-2; these are additional outcomes, not same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, Proposition 1, the Gauss-Newton corollary and the derivations and proofs in Appendices A–B retain their mathematical substance. Corollary 1 becomes Corollary 2, and Equation (1) clarifies approximate-minimizer notation without changing the formulation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a further-training sensitivity standard, a unified interpretation of gradient-based methods, and contrasting approximation behavior of first- and second-order methods. v2 foregrounds the name FiMODA and sensitivity-versus-contribution distinction, but that distinction was already explicit in v1's Section 3.

C2.justification: The expanded Section 7 and appendices explain TRAK's weak results through its single-checkpoint restriction and the different evaluation target. They add computational tradeoffs involving fewer seeds and parameter-efficient tuning, a saturation-related sensitivity limitation, and interpretations of the new detection and qualitative examples. Several original future-work points are retained through relocation.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a project code link, asset-license information and substantially clearer computing-cost disclosure, including approximately 3000 GPU-hours overall and component timings in Appendix D.6. These supplement the already detailed implementation and hyperparameter information in v1.

R1.justification: Table 1 and Appendix C make comparisons with existing retrospective studies more explicit. New references address efficient ensembles, influential-subset selection, mirrored influence and attribution through unlearning synthesized images. The central positioning remains unchanged; the Arnoldi discussion is relocated rather than removed.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction sharpen the framing and introduce FiMODA terminology. Section 7 becomes a structured discussion, while averaging details, the Arnoldi description and some future-work material move to appendices. Most methodological, theoretical and experimental prose retains the original organization and wording.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a compact NeurIPS layout with revised typography and author presentation, wraps text around Figures 1 and 3, and adds two tables and new Figures 6 and 11. The original six-panel Figure 3 moves intact to Figure 7, with two panels retained in the main text. Existing numerical plots are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper with a metric-robustness check, validation against deliberately corrupted labels, and a direct retraining contrast. The code link, compute accounting and expanded limitations also improve reproducibility and interpretation. These are useful but bounded gains: validation still uses restricted training subsets, and the original weak approximation results for non-tabular models remain unresolved.
